title: Legislative rules, statutory grants, and enforcement consequences
shortTitle: Legislative rules, statutory grants, and enforcement consequences
summary: A legislative rule exercises delegated authority to establish a binding standard; an agency must identify a statutory grant and follow the applicable rulemaking procedure.
notes:
The chapter introduction contrasts judicial review of agency rules with review of legislation. Delegated policymaking is subject to procedural scrutiny, evidentiary support, and explanation requirements that do not simply follow from legislative procedure. The editors connect that difference to the APA and to concern about the political accountability of administrators.

The authority question asks whether Congress empowered the agency to adopt substantive standards with legal effect. The procedural question asks how the agency must exercise that power. National Petroleum illustrates their interaction: a binding octane rule narrowed later enforcement to compliance with the rule, whereas a nonbinding statement of the agency’s view would not eliminate the need to prove that a practice violated the statutory standard.

The decision reads § 6(g) broadly and treats § 5 adjudication as an enforcement mechanism compatible with prior general rules. The editorial critique examines a narrower reading based on § 6’s investigative and reporting context, decades of agency practice, and the significance of hiding expansive authority in an ancillary clause. It connects the debate to statutory structure and nondelegation, while keeping those questions distinct from the efficiency case for rulemaking.

The account of the rulemaking expansion in the 1960s and 1970s distinguishes judicial recognition of authority under older general clauses from Congress’s explicit grants in modern regulatory laws. A general clause may also be limited by more specific statutory provisions addressing the same subject. The legal inquiry is source-specific: usefulness of a rule is a reason to examine the grant, not an independent source of power.
